title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) to measure whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑generated NetOps configurations. The frozen design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete paired units (400 episodes); model_calls_used=200 and repair calls invoked=0. Results: baseline 200/200 oracle passes; guarded 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The null outcome is design‑bound: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics delivered identical passing candidates to both arms and never exercised repair. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and give artifact‑grounded recommendations for informative follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are being explored as intent→configuration agents for network operations because they map natural‑language intent into vendor-specific CLI sequences and programmatic device changes. Operational safety requires objective guarantees (for example, transient reachability constraints, protected interfaces, and make‑before‑break semantics) that unconstrained generation does not enforce. A common architectural response is generate→validate→repair: generator proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator (oracle) verifies safety and policy predicates in an emulated model, and a repair module attempts corrective generation if the oracle fails. Prior work reports gains from constraint‑guided generation and verifier‑guided repair, but reproducible, preregistered, artifact‑anchored comparisons remain scarce.

We designed study‑cnd‑2026‑001 to provide a confirmatory, fully archived measurement of verifier assistance under a precisely specified experimental plan. The preregistration froze: the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), sampling plan (Npairs=200), generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), repair budget (≤1), and statistical analysis (paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, and scoring artifacts were archived with SHA‑256 digests for deterministic audit. The central research question: does a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increase oracle pass rate relative to unconstrained generation across the preregistered 200 tasks? The answer under the frozen design is presented below, together with artifact‑grounded diagnostics and reproducible guidance for informative variants.
sections.related_work: LLM‑for‑NetOps research spans intent translation, constrained generation, verifier‑augmented pipelines, and repair loops. Representative leads motivating this work include constraint‑guided NetOps systems and verifier‑grounded repair workflows that emphasize executable validation and counterexample‑driven repair (see cited_record_ids). Prior empirical reports typically evaluate pipelines without a preregistered experimental freeze or without publishing per‑call provider traces and validator traces. Our run differs by preregistering the estimand and generation semantics, executing autonomously, and publishing a comprehensive, hashed artifact bundle (see Execution Manifest and analysis artifacts). This enables a deterministic forensic explanation of why the preregistered comparison returned a null—design interaction—result rather than an absence of verifier value in general.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan (artifacts): We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). The preregistration fixed: primary/secondary estimands, stratified task sampling (200 paired tasks), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generator call per pair, identical candidate delivered to both conditions), declared model = gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1. The immutable initial master prompt that launched the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and is reported in the Disclosure Statement.

Task bank and stratification (artifacts): The preregistered task bank contained 200 paired items stratified by protocol and vendor: protocol buckets BGP/OSPF/ACL/VLAN = 50 pairs each; vendor allocation per protocol Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64); complexity split simple=100 / complex=100. Every task entry (intent, initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, constraints) is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Representative task entries and validator traces are in execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c30860...).

Generation semantics and model configuration (artifacts): Generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (single generator call per pair) intentionally minimized model calls (model_calls_used=200). The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...). All provider call traces and raw responses are recorded under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests listed in execution/execution_manifest.json.

Validator, repair budget, and scoring (artifacts): The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced emulation‑based predicates and produced per‑episode scoring artifacts under execution/scoring/*.json (example: task‑000001 baseline/guarded artifacts). Repair was allowed per preregistration but in this run repair_applied=false for all episodes; no repair traces exist because repair was never invoked. The scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation; the validator traces record parsed_command_count, normalized_configuration, final_state, valid boolean, and violation lists where present.

Execution logging and immutability (artifacts): The autonomous run archived raw responses, provider traces, scoring JSON, task manifest, execution manifest, and analysis outputs, each with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation and provider call audits (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/execution_manifest.json) confirm accounting consistency and the absence of provider drift. Analysis inputs and outputs are in analysis/ with digests (e.g., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...).
sections.results:
Execution summary (artifact‑backed): The preregistered run completed per plan: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared call per pair), repair_calls_invoked=0. Validator acceptance: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (100%); guarded_success_count = 200/200 (100%). The paired contingency is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...).

Primary inference (artifact‑backed): The paired estimate for paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10000, seed=1729). McNemar two‑sided exact test p = 1.00. The complete inferential output and logs are archived in analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 940b48e7...).

Why repair was never observed (artifact causal chain): Under shared_initial_candidate semantics a single generated candidate per pair was supplied identically to both baseline and guarded conditions. The deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate in the task bank; thus the repair stage had zero opportunities to act. Validator traces for representative episodes (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) show validation_after.valid=true and repair_applied=false. The observed null result is therefore a direct consequence of the frozen generation semantics combined with the generator output distribution for these tasks.

Representative examples (artifact excerpts): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 f8de4d6e...) contains the generated candidate; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 eaf96aec...) contains the validator trace showing parsed_command_count=4, required_command_count=4, and valid=true. analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 1cb072b4...) summarizes the 200/200 successes per condition. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...) visually confirms the ceiling effect (all concordant successful pairs).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and scope: The preregistered experiment provides a definitive answer for the frozen estimand under the frozen generation semantics: verifier assistance showed no measured benefit because no repairs were exercisable—the single shared candidate per pair always passed the deterministic oracle. This is a valid empirical outcome for the declared estimand and is fully supported by the archived artifacts and their hashes.

Design lessons and operational implications (artifact‑grounded): The null outcome highlights a key experimental-design dependency: to measure repair efficacy you must (A) allow generator variance between arms (independent generation semantics) or (B) include task items calibrated to elicit validator failures. Two immediate, artifact‑anchored follow‑ups are reproducible from the archive: (1) re‑execute with generation_semantics set to independent_generation (one generator call per condition per pair) which increases model_calls to ≈400 and permits discordant outcomes; (2) augment the task manifest with higher‑difficulty or adversarial tasks (additional dependency constraints or atomic MTU / make‑before‑break rules) so that a nontrivial fraction of generated candidates fail the deterministic validator. Both variants preserve the validator and analysis executor and can be executed using the same adapter; the manifest seeds and task generator id are available in execution/task_manifest.jsonl for deterministic replay.

Threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): Internal validity — preregistered generation semantics produced the ceiling; this choice was explicit and archived (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce925...). Construct validity — deterministic validator enforces emulation predicates but may omit real‑device failure modes; validator traces include coverage diagnostics to flag oracle blind spots. External validity — single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and emulated tasks limit generalization to other models or production images. Conclusion validity — the paired test is exact and reflects the degenerate contingency; confidence intervals and p‑values follow from the observed data and the preregistered analysis plan.

Reproducibility and auditability: The complete artifact set and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json. Key artifacts: preregistration (SHA‑256 a8969ac01f3b...), master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e1805...), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 1acce92558ed...), paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...), representative scoring trace (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 eaf96aec12c3...). To rerun an informative variant, authors should prepare a new preregistration altering generation_semantics or repair budget; the same adapter and validator can be reused and the system will produce an auditable execution_manifest.json for deterministic reconciliation.

Practical recommendation to practitioners: When integrating verifiers in operational agentic stacks, ensure generator variability (distinct samples for guarded vs baseline) or construct workload slices that exercise validator failure modes. Also log and archive all per‑call traces and validator outputs with immutable digests to enable deterministic post‑hoc forensic analysis of agentic behavior in production or evaluation.
sections.conclusion: Under the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic validator, repair budget ≤1), verifier assistance produced no measurable improvement because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the oracle in every case and repairs were never invoked (repair_calls_invoked=0). The study demonstrates that measuring repair efficacy requires aligning generation semantics and task difficulty with the scientific estimand. We publish the full audited artifact bundle (execution/, analysis/, provenance/) so future runs can modify generation semantics or task difficulty while preserving deterministic auditability and reproducibility.

This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 and is the proximate cause repair was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860...). All validator traces are archived and hashed.

Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).

- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs excluded; repair stage not triggered. Full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are included in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the repair stage was never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived and annotated in the artifact bundle.
